output.reason: On its own, the cited item [ev-92063a2a5bac] is just the first entry in a list. The surrounding section [ev-b07a4021f30c] states the change plainly: Loki 3.0 now adds a `service_name` label to all ingested logs by default. Loki builds the value from the first matching label in the ordered list (service_name, service, app, … job; [ev-2690c7915f58] through [ev-ea984d665a12]) and uses `unknown_service` if none match. It also covers who is exposed and how to opt out: logs that already have the label are not reassigned, the list can be changed with `discover_service_name` in limits_config, and an empty value turns the behaviour off. That gives the subject (default label assignment), the change (new default behaviour), the applicability (any ingest unless `discover_service_name` is empty) and the consequence (ingested logs get a new label).
